## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Add coverage for adopting a value that already matches the file. Without that case, the tests would pass if adoption stopped recording matching keys and skipped writing the configuration.

## Changes

The settings merger gains an `adopt` flag that records existing keys and writes the merged configuration even when their values already match. Replacement continues to record existing keys only when their values differ.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/config.py:13 — tests — Cover adoption when the value already matches — With `adopt=True` and `theme` already set to `"dark"`, a regression could omit `"theme"` from the change list and skip the write without failing a test. The adoption test starts with `"light"`. — The tests would miss a regression where matching settings disappear from the list of adopted keys and the configuration write is skipped.

## Suggestions

- app/config.py:18 — tests — Cover existing settings with both modes off — With both flags omitted, a regression could overwrite a stored `"light"` theme with an incoming `"dark"` theme without failing a test. The default-mode test starts with an empty configuration. — The tests would miss a regression that overwrites users’ existing settings during a default merge.
